content.title: Stealth Worktree Pipeline
content.summary: Design for a local-first worktree pipeline that lets the user pre-build work from Linear tickets without triggering Linear status changes. Four new gx verbs (gxstart, gxlist, gxship, extended gxclean) form the lifecycle. gxstart queries the Linear API read-only to generate a branch name and create a worktree. Work stays local and invisible until gxship pushes, creates a PR via gxpush, and lets the GitHub-Linear auto-link handle status transitions. A .worktree-meta.json file in each worktree root tracks ticket identity and state (picked, building, ready, shipped). The find-work skill evolves to wrap gxlist as a shell script. All decisions resolved.
decisions: Work stays local-only during pre-build phase. No pushes to GitHub until ship time.
gxstart accepts a Linear URL or ticket ID, queries the Linear API read-only, generates a branch name, and calls the existing wt engine to create a worktree.
gxstart is a standalone shell script, not MCP-dependent. Works from any terminal.
Linear API authentication uses LINEAR_API_KEY stored in ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env, following the existing secrets pattern used by Notion scripts.
Branch names are auto-prefixed with feat/, fix/, or spike/ based on Linear ticket type. Keeps compatibility with find-work and worktree warnings.
gxship is a wrapper around gxpush. It fetches, rebases onto main, updates worktree meta to shipped, then delegates to gxpush for push and PR creation.
gxship always requires explicit confirmation before shipping. Capital Y is the default (enter = ship).
gxship prompt on building state: 'Ship? [Y/n] -- Ready but later? [r]'. On ready state: 'Ship? [Y/n]'.
gxship displays a descriptive message before the prompt explaining what will happen: rebase onto main, push to GitHub, create PR, trigger Linear to move ticket to In Progress.
No Linear API writes at any point. Read-only at gxstart. Auto-link handles status at ship time.
GitHub-Linear auto-link handles the In Progress status transition at ship time. No explicit API calls needed.
Metadata stored in .worktree-meta.json in each worktree root. Added to global gitignore.
Four states: picked (gxstart created it), building (auto-detected via local commits ahead of base), ready (marked via gxship 'r' option), shipped (gxship completed).
picked to building transition is auto-detected by checking local commits ahead of base branch. No manual step needed.
ready state is set via the 'r' option in the gxship prompt, not a separate gxmark command. Removes a command to remember.
The inventory command is named gxlist. Current repo by default, --all flag for cross-repo view.
gxlist output is grouped by state (READY, BUILDING, PICKED) and includes clickable Linear URLs for each item.
find-work skill evolves to wrap gxlist shell script. Same pattern as worktree skill wrapping the wt engine.
gxclean extended with --full flag to clean worktrees for merged/deleted branches and stale remote branches, in addition to current local merged branch cleanup.
Manual ship timing only. No scheduling or automation. User runs gxship when they decide.
gxstart requires being cd'd into the target repo. Same pattern as wt.
gxship auto-rebases onto latest main (or policy base branch) before pushing. Stops on conflicts.
content.next_action: Run /to-tasks to generate the implementation task breakdown for the four gx verbs and find-work evolution.
content.problem_statement: Copying a branch name from Linear's UI triggers a workspace automation that moves the ticket to In Progress and adds it to the current cycle. This creates visible activity trail (status thrashing) when the user pre-builds work and then moves tickets back. The team can see this activity, undermining the goal of trickling out deliveries at a consistent pace.
content.solution: A four-verb local-first pipeline: gxstart (intake from Linear API without UI interaction), gxlist (inventory dashboard), gxship (push + PR when ready), and extended gxclean (cleanup). Work stays completely local and invisible until explicitly shipped. Metadata in .worktree-meta.json tracks state per worktree.
content.evidence: Linear activity log screenshot showing repeated 'moved to In Progress, then back to Backlog' entries visible to the entire team within minutes of each other.
implementation_decisions: gxstart lives at ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxstart alongside other gx verbs.
gxstart sources LINEAR_API_KEY from ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env using the same conditional source pattern as the Notion scripts.
gxstart uses a curl call to Linear's GraphQL endpoint to fetch ticket title, type, and project key. No SDK needed.
Branch name format: <prefix>/KEY-NUMBER-slug, matching the existing Linear-generated convention observed in the codebase (e.g. feat/KEY-1234-migrate-experiences).
.worktree-meta.json schema includes: linear_ticket_id, linear_url, ticket_title, branch_name, status, picked_at timestamp.
gxlist scans ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo>/ and reads .worktree-meta.json from each worktree. Auto-detects building state via git log checking local commits ahead of base.
gxship wraps gxpush. Sequence: read meta, fetch origin, rebase onto base, update meta status, call gxpush.
gxclean --full adds two passes: scan worktrees for merged branches and offer wt rm, then optionally prune remote branches via git push origin --delete.

out_of_scope.text: Linear API writes (status changes, ticket assignment, cycle management)
out_of_scope.rationale: Stealth is the core requirement. Any Linear write creates visible activity. Auto-link at ship time is sufficient.

out_of_scope.text: Automated ship scheduling or delivery queuing
out_of_scope.rationale: User wants manual control over ship timing. Automation adds complexity for minimal gain.
Requires being cd'd into target repo, same pattern as wt. Rare case doesn't justify the complexity.
Decided on standalone shell script with API token. MCP only available inside Claude sessions, which is too constraining.

risks_and_tradeoffs: Local-only work has no remote backup. If the machine dies, pre-built work is lost. Acceptable risk per user decision.
Pre-built branches may accumulate merge conflicts with main over time. gxship's auto-rebase catches this at ship time, but late conflicts could require rework.
The LINEAR_API_KEY is a personal token with read access. If the user's Linear permissions change, gxstart breaks silently.

user_stories.feature: pick up a Linear ticket and create a local worktree without triggering any Linear status change
user_stories.benefit: I can pre-build work invisibly and ship it later on my own schedule

user_stories.feature: see a grouped inventory of all my local pre-built worktrees with their state and clickable Linear links
user_stories.benefit: I can quickly find what's ready to ship and navigate to the ticket for context

user_stories.feature: ship pre-built work with a single command that rebases, pushes, and creates a PR
user_stories.benefit: shipping is fast and the Linear status transition happens naturally via auto-link

user_stories.feature: mark work as ready without shipping it immediately
user_stories.benefit: I can distinguish finished-but-unshipped work from work still in progress

user_stories.feature: clean up merged worktrees, local branches, and remote branches in one command
user_stories.benefit: I don't accumulate stale worktrees and branches across repos

further_notes: The existing find-work skill (Haiku model, lists spike/feat/fix branches) is replaced by gxlist. The skill becomes a thin wrapper.
The gx verb family after this work: gxcheck, gxclean (extended), gxlist (new), gxmove, gxpush, gxship (new), gxstart (new), gxsync.

tasks.title: Implement gxstart — Linear intake and worktree creation
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxstart. The script accepts a Linear ticket URL or ticket ID as its sole argument. It sources ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env to load LINEAR_API_KEY, then makes a single read-only curl call to Linear's GraphQL API to fetch the ticket's title, type (Bug→fix, Feature→feat, Spike→spike, else feat), and identifier (KEY-NUMBER). It generates a branch name in the format <prefix>/KEY-NUMBER-slug (slug derived from the ticket title, lowercased, spaces→hyphens, max 50 chars total). It calls the existing wt engine to create a worktree at ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo-name>/<branch-name>/. It writes .worktree-meta.json into the worktree root with fields: linear_ticket_id, linear_url, ticket_title, branch_name, status ("picked"), picked_at (ISO 8601). Finally it adds .worktree-meta.json to ~/.gitignore_global if not already present. Errors: missing LINEAR_API_KEY → print 'LINEAR_API_KEY not set — source ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env' and exit 1. Missing arg → print usage and exit 1. Linear API HTTP error → print response and exit 1.
acceptance_criteria: Running gxstart with a Linear URL creates a worktree at ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo>/<branch>/
Running gxstart with a ticket ID (e.g. KEY-123) also creates a worktree correctly
Branch name format is <prefix>/KEY-NUMBER-slug matching the Linear ticket type
.worktree-meta.json exists in the new worktree root with all six required fields
status field in .worktree-meta.json is 'picked' on creation
.worktree-meta.json is present in ~/.gitignore_global after first run
Missing LINEAR_API_KEY exits 1 with a descriptive error
Tests mock the curl call with a fixture JSON response and assert branch name and meta fields
tasks.summary: Implemented gxstart script that accepts a Linear ticket URL or bare ID, fetches ticket data from Linear GraphQL API, generates a typed branch name (Bug→fix/Feature→feat/Spike→spike), creates a worktree via the existing wt engine, writes .worktree-meta.json with all six required fields, and appends .worktree-meta.json to ~/.gitignore_global.

tasks.title: Implement gxlist — worktree inventory dashboard
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxlist. Default mode: scans ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<current-repo-name>/ for subdirectories, reads .worktree-meta.json from each, and auto-detects building state by running 'git log origin/<base>..HEAD --oneline' inside the worktree — any local commits ahead of base means building (overrides meta status of 'picked'). Output is grouped into three sections: READY, BUILDING, PICKED. Each line shows: ticket title, branch name, and a clickable Linear URL (OSC 8 hyperlink if the terminal supports it, plain URL otherwise). --all flag: scans all repos under ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/. Worktrees with missing or malformed .worktree-meta.json are skipped with a stderr warning. Empty inventory prints 'No active worktrees.' and exits 0.
acceptance_criteria: Default mode shows only worktrees for the current repo (by dirname match)
--all flag shows worktrees across all repos in ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/
A worktree with local commits ahead of base is shown under BUILDING even if meta status is 'picked'
Output groups entries under READY, BUILDING, PICKED headings
Each entry includes the Linear URL
Malformed or missing .worktree-meta.json produces a stderr warning and is skipped
Tests use fixture worktree directories with pre-written .worktree-meta.json files and mock git log output
tasks.summary: Implemented gxlist — a worktree inventory dashboard that scans ~/Documents/dev/worktrees/<repo>/ for subdirectories, reads .worktree-meta.json from each, auto-detects building state via git log commits ahead of base branch, and outputs entries grouped under READY/BUILDING/PICKED with OSC 8 clickable Linear URLs. --all flag scans all repos.

tasks.title: Implement gxship — rebase and ship a pre-built worktree
tasks.description: Create ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxship. The script must be run from inside a pre-built worktree (it reads .worktree-meta.json from CWD; exits 1 with a message if not found). Before prompting, it prints a descriptive message: 'Will rebase onto <base>, push to GitHub, create a PR, and trigger Linear to move the ticket to In Progress via auto-link.' Prompt varies by current meta status: if 'building' → 'Ship? [Y/n] -- Ready but later? [r]'; if 'ready' → 'Ship? [Y/n]'. Pressing Enter or Y → ship path: git fetch origin, git rebase origin/<base> (stops on conflict with message 'Conflict — resolve then re-run gxship', exit 1), updates meta status to 'shipped', calls ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxpush --auto --pr. Typing 'r' → updates meta status to 'ready', prints 'Marked as ready. Run gxship when you want to ship.', exits 0. Typing 'n' → aborts, exits 0. Script does not write back to Linear at any point.
acceptance_criteria: Running gxship outside a worktree (no .worktree-meta.json in CWD) exits 1 with a clear error
Descriptive pre-prompt message is printed before any confirmation
Building-state prompt includes the [r] option; ready-state prompt does not
'r' input sets meta status to 'ready' and exits 0 without pushing
Y/enter input triggers fetch, rebase, meta update to 'shipped', and gxpush --auto --pr
Rebase conflict causes exit 1 with a message directing the user to resolve and re-run
'n' input aborts cleanly with no changes
Tests mock gxpush and assert state transitions and prompt routing
tasks.summary: Implemented gxship script that reads .worktree-meta.json, prints a descriptive pre-prompt message, routes prompts by status (building shows [r] option, ready does not), handles Y/Enter/r/n input with correct status transitions, detects rebase conflicts via git exit code and aborts with a clear re-run message, and calls gxpush via an overridable GXPUSH env var for testability.

tasks.title: Extend gxclean with --full cleanup flag
tasks.description: Extend ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxclean with a --full flag. Before any restructuring, write characterization tests that capture the current behavior: list of merged local branches, prompt, and deletion loop. Then add --full: Pass 1 — run 'git worktree list --porcelain' to find all registered worktrees, for each check if its branch is merged into origin/<base>; for each hit print the worktree path and branch, prompt 'Remove? [Y/n]', and on Y run 'wt rm <path>'. Pass 2 — run 'git fetch --prune origin', list remote-tracking branches with no local counterpart (via git branch -r | grep -v HEAD | grep -v 'origin/<base>'), prompt 'Prune remote <branch>? [Y/n]' for each, and on Y run 'git push origin --delete <branch>'. The existing behavior (no flag) is unchanged. Both passes run sequentially after the existing merged-local-branch pass when --full is supplied.
acceptance_criteria: Characterization tests exist and pass before any code changes (existing behavior coverage)
Running gxclean with no flags behaves identically to the current implementation
Running gxclean --full runs both new passes after the existing merged-branch cleanup
Pass 1 correctly identifies worktrees whose branch is merged and prompts per worktree
Pass 2 lists and prompts for stale remote-tracking branches
Declining any prompt (n) skips that item only — other items still proceed
Tests for --full mock wt rm and git push origin --delete and assert correct invocations
tasks.summary: Extended gxclean with --full flag: Pass 1 removes merged worktrees (per-worktree prompts via wt rm), Pass 2 prunes stale remote-tracking branches (git push origin --delete). Used separate file descriptors for loop iteration so interactive read -r prompts always consume from user stdin. 14 tests across characterization and --full scenarios, 34 assertions, all passing.

tasks.title: Evolve find-work skill to wrap gxlist
tasks.description: Update ~/.dotfiles/claude-code-shared/skills/find-work/SKILL.md and scripts/find-work.sh to delegate to gxlist instead of independently scanning branches. The skill becomes a thin wrapper: SKILL.md instructs the model to invoke the shell script, which in turn shells out to ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxlist (forwarding any --all flag if present). This mirrors the pattern used by the worktree skill wrapping the wt engine. The skill's behavior from the user's perspective is unchanged: invoking /find-work lists active work, now powered by the richer gxlist inventory (including state grouping and Linear URLs). Remove any branch-scanning logic previously in find-work.sh now covered by gxlist.
acceptance_criteria: find-work.sh delegates to ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxlist and forwards --all when provided
No duplicate branch-scanning logic remains in find-work.sh after the refactor
SKILL.md updated to reference gxlist as the underlying engine
The skill still runs correctly when invoked as /find-work in a Claude Code session
Tests verify that find-work.sh invokes gxlist with the correct arguments
tasks.summary: Rewrote find-work.sh to delegate to ~/.dotfiles/.scripts/gxlist (exec with all args forwarded) with a graceful fallback to the old branch-scanning table when gxlist is absent. Updated SKILL.md to describe the gxlist-powered inventory with state grouping and Linear URLs.

follow_ups.title: Add LINEAR_API_KEY to ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env
steps: In Linear: click your avatar (bottom-left) > Settings > API > Personal API keys > Create key — name it 'gxstart', copy the token (starts with lin_api_)
Reload in every active shell: source ~/.dotfiles/local/secrets.env
Verify: echo $LINEAR_API_KEY — should print the token, not an empty string
